questions.question: Set up an equation for a taxi charging R12 plus R8 per km whose trip cost R60, and interpret each part.
questions.expected_answer: Let k be the kilometres. 8k + 12 = 60. The 8 is the rate per km, 8k the distance charge, 12 the once-off flag fee, 8k + 12 the fare, and 60 what the trip cost.

questions.question: Why must the variable be defined in a sentence before the equation is written?
questions.expected_answer: The letter has no meaning until it is defined; the definition earns a mark and prevents answering the wrong question — for example giving k = 6 as six rand instead of six kilometres.

questions.question: Explain why 300g + 40 = 900 is a wrong set-up for a party with a R300 venue and R40 per guest.
questions.expected_answer: It makes 300 the per-guest cost and 40 the once-off cost, the reverse of the situation. The coefficient of g must be the per-guest amount: 40g + 300 = 900.
